correctness.rationale: The feature operator B_ε is Hilbert–Schmidt, since its squared norm is ε∫ζ(1+2εa)dν≤I+εM by integral comparison. H_ε=B_ε*B_ε and K_ε=B_εB_ε* have the same positive eigenvalues with multiplicity, also for a finite-dimensional L²(ν). The continuous Laplace feature u_t(a)=exp(−at) gives K_ν as a trace-class Bochner integral with ∫||u_t||²dt=I. For the logarithmic mesh t_n=ε log n, the excess positive weight ε/n−(t_(n+1)−t_n) sums to ε γ_E, hence costs at most ε γ_E M in trace norm. With h=ε log 2, the mesh left endpoint τ(t) lies between max(0,t−h) and t. For each a>0 the integral of exp(−a max(0,t−h))−exp(−at) is exactly h, and the same holds with a replaced by 2a. Since squared differences on [0,1] are bounded by differences, the squared feature discrepancy integrates to at most hM and the quadrature's trace is at most I+hM. Factoring the rank-one difference and using Cauchy–Schwarz gives exactly sqrt((4I+2hM)hM). The trace-ideal eigenvalue inequality transfers this to the ordered zero-padded lists. The zeta pole-subtracted function is bounded between zero and one and tends to γ_E, giving the trace residue by dominated convergence without a positive moment. Positivity and the uniform trace bound turn each vanishing diagonal entry into ||H_ε e_n||→0, extending by density. Spectral convergence gives a positive limiting norm because I>0. The atomic Cauchy matrix and classical determinant use the orthonormal measure coordinates. Analytic replay: frozen RESULT.md lines 35–105. The supplied script and requirements describe only finite-atomic diagnostics; the code was inspected, not executed. The O(√ε) estimate is not an optimality claim: for n≥2 the bound sup_(a>0) a exp(−at_n)=1/(e t_n) even gives interval error ≤M(t_(n+1)−t_n)²/(e t_n), summable with total O(εM) after separately bounding the first interval. This does not invalidate the stated estimate.

value.rationale: This is a natural boundary-scaling limit for positive multiplicative moment operators. All spectral mass and operator norms are tracked even though each fixed coordinate vanishes; compactness of support, density, and higher moments are unnecessary. The comparison supplies a measure-uniform quantitative control under the trace-class integrability requirement and converts singular or atomic input measures into explicit limiting operators. Its utility is the full trace-ideal control, not the standard trace identity or an assertion that the stated rate is sharp.
